prompt: Company profile: Custom metal fabricator in Tulsa, Oklahoma; 55 employees. Situation: The shop is taking on stainless-steel work for food-equipment customers: TIG and MIG welding plus plasma cutting of 304/316 stainless, roughly 20 hours of arc time per day across six welders. Welding on stainless can generate hexavalent chromium fume. Current ventilation is general dilution only. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
**Compliance Obligations Register – Hexavalent Chromium (CrVI) from Stainless-Steel Welding** *Company: Custom Metal Fabricator, Tulsa, OK (55 employees)* --- ### **Obligation 1: OSHA Permissible Exposure Limit (PEL) & Exposure Assessment** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Ensure no employee is exposed to CrVI at concentrations >5 µg/m³ as an 8-hour TWA or >2.5 µg/m³ action level. Conduct initial exposure determination via personal air monitoring for each job classification (e.g., TIG/MIG welders, plasma cutters). If exposures are at/above action level, implement periodic monitoring at least every 6 months; if below, at least every 12 months. Re-assess when process/equipment changes. | | **Source** | 29 CFR 1910.1026(d) – Hexavalent Chromium Standard (OSHA) | | **Applicability** | Directly applies. With ~20 hours daily arc time on 304/316 stainless across six welders, CrVI fume generation is certain. General dilution ventilation alone is unlikely to maintain exposures below PEL, triggering mandatory monitoring and control obligations. | | **ISO Clause** | ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements – health hazards) | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | **How:** Industrial hygiene sampling by a qualified CIH or trained staff using NIOSH Method 7605; statistical analysis of results; compare to PEL/AL. Document in exposure assessment report.
**When:** Initial within 30 days of startup of stainless work; then per the periodic schedule (6 or 12 months based on results); immediately after any process change; annually at minimum via management review. | --- ### **Obligation 2: Engineering & Work Practice Controls (Ventilation Upgrade)** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Implement feasible engineering controls (e.g., local exhaust ventilation (LEV) at source, downdraft tables, fume extraction MIG guns) to reduce CrVI exposures below PEL. General dilution ventilation is not considered a primary control. Use work practices like minimizing weld current, avoiding unnecessary arcing, and positioning hoods within 1–2 hood diameters of the weld point. | | **Source** | 29 CFR 1910.1026(f) – Methods of Compliance; 1910.1026(e) – Regulated Areas | | **Applicability** | Critical. Current general dilution is insufficient for CrVI. Six welders generating fume simultaneously will exceed PEL without LEV. Must install/source-capture systems and designate regulated areas where exposures exceed PEL. | | **ISO Clause** | ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements – hierarchy of controls) | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | **How:** Pre-/post-installation air monitoring; visual inspection of LEV function (hood velocity, static pressure checks per ACGIH/ANSI Z9.2); employee feedback; maintenance logs review.
**When:** Before stainless work begins (baseline); within 15 days of installing new controls; quarterly inspections of LEV performance; during 9.1.2 compliance audits; after any ventilation modification. | --- ### **Obligation 3: Medical Surveillance Program** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Offer medical surveillance at no cost to employees exposed >30 days/year at/above action level (2.5 µg/m³). Includes initial medical exam (work history, physical, chest X-ray, pulmonary function test) within 30 days of assignment; periodic exams annually; and exit exam. Provide physician’s written opinion and copy to employee. | | **Source** | 29 CFR 1910.1026(k) – Medical Surveillance | | **Applicability** | Applies if exposure monitoring shows levels ≥2.5 µg/m³. With 20 hours/day arc time, it is highly probable welders will exceed this threshold, triggering mandatory program. | | **ISO Clause** | ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements – health monitoring) | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | **How:** Audit medical surveillance roster vs. exposure data; review physician certifications and exam records (maintain confidentiality); track participation rates; verify physician written opinions are provided.
**When:** Within 30 days of assigning employee to stainless welding; annually thereafter; during 9.1.2 compliance audit (minimum annually); upon employee request. | --- ### **Obligation 4: Hazard Communication & Training** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Train welders on CrVI hazards (cancer, respiratory irritation), PEL/AL, control measures, PPE, hygiene, and medical surveillance. Provide SDS for welding consumables; post warning signs in regulated areas (“WARNING – HEXAVALENT CHROMIUM – CANCER HAZARD”). Training at initial assignment and annually. | | **Source** | 29 CFR 1910.1026(l) – Communication of Hazards; 1910.1200 (HCS) | | **Applicability** | Directly applies to all six welders and affected workers (e.g., supervisors, maintenance). Must be completed before stainless work begins. | | **ISO Clause** | ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements – worker communication) | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | **How:** Review training records for completion/dates; interview employees for comprehension; inspect posted signage; audit SDS accessibility.
**When:** Before initial stainless welding; annually per standard; during new-hire onboarding; during 9.1.2 audit (minimum annually). | --- ### **Obligation 5: Recordkeeping & Reporting** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Maintain exposure monitoring records (date, duration, method, results, employee identifiers) for 30 years. Maintain medical surveillance records for duration of employment + 30 years. Provide records to employees, OSHA, and NIOSH on request. Report any CrVI exposure resulting in medical treatment >first aid on OSHA 300 Log. | | **Source** | 29 CFR 1910.1026(m) – Recordkeeping; 29 CFR 1904 – Injury/Illness Recording | | **Applicability** | Applies to all monitoring and medical data generated from the stainless-steel work. | | **ISO Clause** | ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (Legal & other requirements – documented information) | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | **How:** Internal audit of record completeness, retention, and confidentiality; cross-check OSHA 300 Log entries against medical surveillance outcomes.
**When:** Quarterly record review by EHS manager; annually during 9.1.2 compliance audit; within 5 days of employee/OSHA request. | --- ### **Obligation 6: Environmental Release & Waste Management** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Evaluate if CrVI-contaminated filters/dust from ventilation systems constitute hazardous waste under Oklahoma DEQ rules (OAC 252:205). If characteristic (e.g., TCLP >5 mg/L Cr), manage as D007 hazardous waste per EPA RCRA (40 CFR 262). Report releases of CrVI compounds >1 lb/24 hrs under EPCRA 304/CERCLA 103. | | **Source** | Oklahoma DEQ OAC 252:205; EPA 40 CFR 262 (RCRA); EPCRA 304/CERCLA 103 | | **Applicability** | Applies if LEV generates concentrated CrVI particulate. A small fabricator may be a CESQG (Conditionally Exempt Small Quantity Generator) but must still determine waste status. Release reporting unlikely but must be assessed. | | **ISO Clause** | ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3 (Environmental compliance obligations) | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | **How:** Waste characterization testing (TCLP) of filters/dust; review waste vendor manifests; calculate potential release quantities; check DEQ permit exemptions.
**When:** Before first waste shipment; annually for waste status; during 9.1.2 environmental compliance audit; immediately after any spill/release. | --- ### **Summary Evaluation Schedule for 9.1.2** | **Evaluation Activity** | **Frequency** | **Method** | |---------------------------|---------------|------------| | Exposure monitoring | Initial + 6/12 months | Industrial hygiene sampling | | LEV performance check | Quarterly | Velocity/pressure measurements | | Medical surveillance roster audit | Monthly | HR/EHS record cross-check | | Training compliance | Monthly | Training record review | | Recordkeeping audit | Quarterly | Document review | | Full compliance audit (all obligations) | **Annually** | Internal audit per ISO 9.1.2 | | Management review of compliance status | Annually | Management review meeting | **Note:** Oklahoma is a federal OSHA state; no state-plan deviations apply. All obligations are mandatory and non-compliance can result in citations ($7,000–$70,000+ per violation), worker illness claims, and environmental penalties.
